textbookText: 2. Division of the body The body of an adult frog is divisible into head and trunk with limbs. Neck and tail are absent. i. Head: The head is flat and roughly triangular in outline, with a short and less blunt anterior snout. A wide transverse opening is situated at the anterior end of the snout, called mouth. There are two small openings lying dorsally above the mouth called external nostrils or external nares which serve in breathing. A pair of spherical and bulging eyes, each situated at the dorso-lateral position on the top of the head. Bulging eye helps to see all possible direction in the absence of neck. Each eye has thick and pigmented upper eye lid and a thin and semitransparent lower eyelid. Upper eyelid is immovable whereas lower eye lid is movable. Both the eyes of frog have nictitating membrane (plica semilunaris) arising from the lower eyelid, which protect eyes in water from foreign substances and also prevent drying of eye in terrestrial habitat. In front of eyes lie a light coloured brow spot which represents vestigial pineal eye. Just behind the eye on each side, a circular and pigmented tympanum is present which receives sound waves but external ear is absent in frog. In male frogs, two bluish and wrinkled vocal sacs are present on the undersurface of throat, used to produce croaking sounds in the breeding season for attracting female frog. ii. Trunk: Trunk is a flat and oval structure which is joined directly with the head. During resting or squatting condition, posterior side of trunk, in the middle is slightly raised forming hump which is also called sacral prominence. There is a small circular opening called vent or cloacal aperture at the posterior end of trunk between hind limbs. This aperture is the common for discharging out faeces, urine and gametes.

There are two pairs of limbs arising laterally from the trunk. Anterior pair is called forelimbs, which arise just behind the head. Each forelimb consists of proximal upper arm (brachium), fore arm (antebrachium), wrist (carpus) and hand (manus) bearing 4 fingers or digits where thumb is externally invisible or rudimentary. Fingers of forelimbs are without fold of skin or web between them. In the case of male frog, base of index or first finger is thickened to form nuptial pad or amplexuary pad or copulatory pad to hold the female frog firmly during amplex or copulation. Posterior pair is hind limbs which are comparatively much longer and powerful than fore limbs. Each hind limb consists of proximal thigh, middle shank, a long ankle or tarsus and large foot bearing five fingers with a fold of skin in between, called webbed toes used in swimming. Undersurface of digits of forelimb and hind limb contains small and round pads called sub-articular pads which are shock absorber and also aid in gripping and climbing surfaces.

Sexual dimorphism Sexual dimorphism is the condition or phenomenon in which male and female of same animal species are distinguished by observing their external features. Sexual dimorphism is relatively more distinct in the breeding season in Rana tigrina. In copulating frogs, upper one is male and the lower one is female.
